copy.title: proof
copy.solHome: a thought is a guess about real life. an experiment checks the guess, and whatever turns up is proof.
copy.openNote: these can wait as long as they like. no clock on them.
copy.proofEmpty: nothing here yet. whatever turns up in an experiment can live here.
copy.thanks: thanks for being curious about this.
copy.sourceAsk: where will today's experiment come from?
copy.sourceLead: a thought to test, in real life, today. you pick the size.
copy.sourceTeach: an experiment treats a thought as a guess, then tries something small to see what happens (Bennett-Levy et al., 2004).
copy.fromLadder: a rung from one rung up
copy.voiceHint: the words stay on this phone, and only show when tapped.
copy.claimAsk: what does the inner voice predict?
copy.claimSol: of course it has a view. it's been trying to look out for things. a guess is easy to check.
copy.predictSol: an honest guess is the best start. any guess is a fine one.
copy.planAsk: what's the small thing to do?
copy.believeAsk: how true does it feel right now?
copy.believeNote: just a reading, so there's something to look back at. nothing to get right.
copy.again: this one has come up before. proof already gathered:
copy.doneSol: thank you. that's real courage, and it's small on purpose. there's nothing to do until it happens, and it's fine if the day takes over.
copy.doneNote: this evening, home will have a card to look back. it can wait, too.
copy.eveningAsk: thanks for trying something real today. what happened?

happened.label: it went the way the voice said
happened.reply: thank you for saying so. that's useful to know, and it's one try on one day.

happened.label: it went differently
happened.reply: good to know. that's worth keeping.

happened.label: somewhere in between
happened.reply: most real days are. the in-between counts.

happened.label: i didn't get to it
happened.reply: that's fine. it can stay open, or go.

copy.keepAsk: anything here worth keeping as proof?
copy.keepTeach: the mind holds hard moments tighter than good ones (Baumeister et al., 2001). writing down what turned up helps it count.
copy.keepPlaceholder: what turned up, in a sentence
copy.keptSol: kept. it's in the book now.
copy.believeAgain: and how true does it feel now?
copy.believeWas: it was {n} of 100 this morning. any number is fine.
copy.closeAsk: what happens to this experiment now?
copy.closeOpenNote: it stays open as long as it likes.
copy.closedSol: closed, and whatever turned up is yours.
copy.letGoSol: let go. no strings. it was a good try.
copy.shiftSol: here's how it moved. any shift counts, and so does none.
copy.reflectDone: thank you for looking back. that took some honesty.
copy.bookNote: things that turned up in real life, in their own words. the thought behind each one stays hidden until tapped.

sourcesList.label: Bennett-Levy et al., 2004
sourcesList.title: Oxford Guide to Behavioural Experiments in Cognitive Therapy
sourcesList.evidence: well used in therapy, mostly with a therapist; less tested as a solo exercise

sourcesList.label: Baumeister et al., 2001
sourcesList.title: Bad is stronger than good
sourcesList.evidence: strong (a large review of many studies)

whyBubbles: a behavioural experiment is a plain idea: treat a thought as a guess, try something small in real life, and see what happens.
therapists have used them for decades (Bennett-Levy et al., 2004). that was with a therapist, so here it's an invitation to try, not a promise.
and the mind holds hard moments tighter than good ones (the negativity bias; Baumeister et al., 2001). so what turns up gets written down here.

claim: if i speak up, they'll think i'm annoying.
if i ask for help, they'll think less of me.
if i say no, they'll be upset with me.
if i try it, i'll make a mess of it.
if i share my idea, it'll land flat.

voice: it'll go the way the voice says.
people will notice and judge it.
i won't be able to do it.
kind: i'll find one moment it was true.
it'll feel true in some places and not in others.

voice: ask for a hand with something small.
say no to one small thing.
kind: notice one moment it was true.
say it quietly before a conversation.

asVoice: i tried it, with the voice talking.
i found out what it feels like to try.
i did it anyway, and that took something.
different: it went better than the voice said.
nobody reacted the way it predicted.
it felt okay once it was done.
someone was glad i did it.
between: it was easier than i expected, in one way.
i got through it, and that's something.
